subject: Private observability: SIEM export options, redaction workflow, and routing
messages:
From: Priya Rao <priya@acmecloud.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: secops-team@acmecloud.com
Date: 2029-05-05T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Private observability: SIEM export, redaction, and routing questions

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the initial onboarding call last week. We're starting to plan the observability export for our VPC-based private deployment and have a few concrete questions so we can map requirements on our side (network/security/compliance) before the handoff: 

1) Transport options: you mentioned Splunk HEC and syslog over TLS. Do you also support a push-based endpoint behind a customer NAT (outbound-only), or does Private require an inbound collector endpoint in our DMZ/Bastion?

2) Redaction & PII controls: can Redwood apply field-level redaction/enrichment at the export boundary, or do we need to perform client-side scrubbing? We need to know where sensitive tokens (SSNs, API keys, e-mails) can be masked for our SOC2 control mapping.

3) SIEM mapping: sample event mappings (Splunk sourcetypes, Elastic ECS fields) would be helpful. Do you provide a canonical CSV or mapping file we can consume in our SIEM onboarding playbook?

4) Tracing hooks/provenance: can trace IDs be preserved across the forwarder, and is there a reliable header/key used for distributed tracing correlation?

5) Auditing & retention: what audit trails are available for export deliveries, and can you provide an example of the evidence package your team would generate for an audit?

I've attached our high-level SIEM requirements (acme_siem_requirements.pdf). Could you point to the minimal network allowlist and any sample redaction rules? Also propose a short window (30–45m) for a technical handoff with your eng/ops team.

Best,

Priya Rao
Senior Security Engineer
Acme Cloud

Attachment: acme_siem_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private observability: SIEM export, redaction, and routing questions

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear list. Passing to the team but wanted to give a short answer and attach a couple of artifacts you can review ahead of the call.

Short answers:
- Transport: Private supports both inbound (customer-facing collector) and outbound-only push models. For outbound-only we run a TLS-encrypted forwarder from your VPC to our signed endpoint; that is usually the least friction for locked-down networks. Inbound collectors are supported via a bastion/DMZ pattern if you need internal tokenization.
- Redaction: We support both client-side and server-side redaction. Recommended pattern: apply deterministic PII scrubbing client-side (customer-managed) and use our export-layer redaction for secondary masking (field suppression, regex-based blacklisting) so you have defense in depth.
- SIEM mapping: attached is a small sample mapping (sample_event_mapping.csv) and a compact guide (redwood_private_obsv_export_guide.pdf) with Splunk HEC examples and ECS-compatible field names.
- Tracing: We propagate x-redwood-trace-id and will preserve trace/span ids through the forwarder. We can also inject a redwood_forwarder.provenance field with the upstream request id.
- Auditing: Export receipts are logged for every batch with delivery status, HMAC of the batch, and sequence numbers. We can produce an evidence package (zipped manifest + signed receipts) for auditors.

Next steps: please pick a 30-minute slot and we'll have Kimberly cover connectivity and Jonas cover SIEM mapping. Proposed times: Tue 2029-05-07 09:00–09:30 PT or Wed 2029-05-08 14:00–14:30 PT.

Attachments: redwood_private_obsv_export_guide.pdf (application/pdf); sample_event_mapping.csv (text/csv)

--
Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Engineer, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Priya — jumping in with the technical specifics you asked for. Below is a concise checklist and examples we use in private engagements. Happy to walk through these on Tuesday.

1) Egress allowlist & certificates
- Typical egress: 3 IPs per region for HA (list provided during onboarding). We provide a TLS certificate chain (Let's Encrypt / customer-trusted CA option) and mutual TLS is available for HEC.
- Action: allow outbound 443 to the three hostnames in the onboarding doc. If you prefer a static IP arrangement we can allocate an Elastic egress endpoint under a reserved capacity agreement.

2) Contextual redaction rules (supported)
- Rule types: field-key suppression, regex, token-class replacement, conditional rules (if payload.source=="user.contact" then mask email pattern).
- Implementation: you can upload a JSON rule bundle or enable a managed rule set. Redaction happens at the exporter plugin level; field-level decisions are evaluated against the event JSON schema.

Example rule (YAML excerpt):
---
- id: mask_user_contact_email
  when:
    - payload.source == "user.contact"
  then:
    - redact: payload.user.email
    - replace_with: "[email_masked]"
---

3) Evidence package sizing
- For a single HEC stream with average 2,000 small events/min (200B/event), 30 days of receipts and batch manifests typically compress to ~5–12 MB depending on batch window and gzip ratio. Full event payload retention size is not part of the evidence package by default; we only include delivery receipts, sequence manifests, and HMACs unless you opt into full archive.

4) Tracing & provenance
- Header: x-redwood-trace-id (64-bit hex) + redwood_forwarder.provenance in the event envelope. We maintain a monotonic batch sequence number in headers for reordering detection.

5) Onboarding playbook & mapping
- We attach the siem_mapping_playbook_v1.yml which includes an example Splunk HEC payload, ECS mapping, and a small transform script you can paste into your ingestion pipeline.

Next: confirmed — Tue 2029-05-07 09:00 PT works. I'll send a calendar invite with a Zoom link and the access checklist in the invite body.

Attachments: siem_mapping_playbook_v1.yml (text/yaml)
